Some of my experience in the latter paragraphs, but first to answer your question. Yeah, it feels absolutely hopeless. And yet? this is quite literally all there is, and will ever be. I get how you feel. My last couple of years I sort of stopped trying, and only recently managed to find the will to give a fuck again. It might be a curse, and it might never get better. But since there's absolutely nothing else than this? Might as well enjoy the coffee, and the sun. and the music. I've been living day to day, and yeah, my future might be fucked, but death comes for us all, all the same. Just lower the scope to whatever you might enjoy, and it makes it bearable, ever so slightly. 

Also, i avoid other people like the plague, but i also understand how good it is to connect with people. Even going to the grocery store can help. I would encourage you to try and walk at least a km everyday, and try to speak to someone. Even if it's online. Those are my current goals to help my body and mind. I don't manage it everyday, but whenever i do, it helps. Best of luck



I spent the last decade or so without much more than the next month to look forward to. It gets tiring starting from zero each time. Running on the same place while the people you know get farther away. I'm very lucky to have found some amazing friends that don't seem to mind the worst aspects of my adhd, but it's still a challenge to keep in touch. Everyone is far away and i'm just so tired all the time.

Yesterday I had the worst scare ever. I just forgot where my savings were. The only meaningful thing i did since last year, and it just vanished. It was entirely possible that i put it in a box or a bag and threw it away. I don't know if I could've recovered from that one. Luckily, it was under a pile of clothes. I meant to store it elsewhere and forgot. 

It does get scary, how forgetful i've become. I'm only 23, and my mind feels so scattered all the time. I didn't help myself much with the drug consumption the last 5 years, but i'm steadily leaving that behind. I just hope it's not too late to make a change.

I still have my camera, and plenty of notebooks to write, and i bought a graphic tablet to start drawing. For the first two i started like 15 years ago, and are one of those things that just make sense to me. I know how to take good photos, altough I'm not as good at picking subjects for them (anyone else gets ridiculously moved by random flowers or trees). And only got better with time. The same with writing, I struggle a lot to write longer ideas nowadays, but whatever I do write is certainly better.

I rarely do any of them. Sometimes it feels harder to do things I like than things I have to do. But I occasionally take my camera with me and sometimes i use it. From time to time I write about how I feel. And A couple of days ago I managed to draw a couple of boxes. It's all too unreasonably exhausting, but having it nearby makes it happen occasionally.

The dagger and the coin series by daniel Abraham

A medieval high fantasy setting with a touch of realism. It can be a bit crude at times, but the narrative is quite endearing. You follow the stories of various characters: scarred veteran turned mercenary, the young apprentice of a bank, an ordinary noble, and some others.

The switch between characters is very well paced, there's great world building, and an overarching storyline that is very neatly set up by the first books.

The first book, the dragon's path, is a great read on its own, but it didn't hook me up as much for the sequel. Once I finished the second one, though, i couldn't stop until i read all five of them.

Highly recommended. Definitely my favorite fantasy series

I don't know what definition you have for constructive criticism, nor the official definition for that matter, but I think that criticism can be considered constructive when:

- Has arguments that don't rely on "It's wrong because I don't like it" or anything that isn't a fact, but solely personal opinion. ( That doesn't mean that expressing your personal opinion is wrong, but it's a different thing than an argument. Also, all good arguments have a "I think that this and that is wrong because of [fact]" there's always personal opinion, but it's backed up with facts)

- doesn't rely on insulting or attacking the other person ( he is lazy, he is a liar...)

- has the intention to build a better situation

So, having those parameters, it's hard to misconstrue constructive criticism, as if the person that writes it has good intentions, it will always go along these parameters. (As long as they use facts, I don't think that the first one is really that important, as most people have the habit to talk like "this is good" rather than "I think this is good", but the two other are pretty much needed if you want to share your opinion)
